Subject: Net-45 Payment Terms Blocked by Coupa Registration — MSA redline coordination

Hi Jill —

Quick note after the conversation with your procurement team this morning: we're seeing the Coupa registration flow flag the vendor as "pending" because the tax ID on the vendor profile doesn't match the W-9 that CuraHealth uploaded. That mismatch is preventing creation of a first PO and procurement is indicating their policy won't allow Net-45 without a formal exception.

We're happy to proceed with MSA + Order Form, but Legal at both sides needs to lock the payment term language so procurement can tie vendor setup to the signed contract. I've attached the latest redline (Redlined-MSA-v3.pdf) and the Order Form draft (OrderForm_CuraHealth_v2.docx) — the only substantive commercial ask from your team is Net-45 on payment terms.

Requested next steps:
- Can your procurement team confirm the exact field causing the tax ID mismatch in Coupa? (tax id/EIN vs. VAT field)
- Can Legal (cc: laura) take a quick look at the Net-45 redline and either approve or propose a short-term compromise (e.g., 30 days + early-pay discount or escrow) so procurement can provision the vendor record?
- Rishi will coordinate the Coupa registration checklist on our side and submit the vendor profile updates once we have an agreed payment term.

I know this is time sensitive for your go-live next week — happy to jump on a quick call if that helps.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan

Hi Tessa —

Thanks for the summary. Quick clarifications from procurement: the Coupa onboarding form has a remit-to VAT field and a tax ID field; our vendor portal requires the EIN in the "Tax ID" field to exactly match the uploaded W-9. If there's a suffix or formatting difference (dashes, leading zeros), the system throws a mismatch and flags the vendor as "pending verification."

Procurement policy: Net-30 is standard. Net-45 requires a documented business justification and a formal exception from finance; we can request that, but it takes 3–5 business days. If you can get Legal to accept a temporary compromise (Net-30 with an agreed escalator or 1% early-pay discount at 20 days), procurement can provision the vendor record "approved for PO issuance under contingent exception" and issue the first PO.

Also see attached Coupa registration guidance — it helps avoid the common field mismatch. I've attached it and cc'd procurement for visibility.

-Jill
Jill Adams
Procurement Manager | CuraHealth
jill.adams@curahealth.com

Subject: Re: Net-45 Payment Terms Blocked by Coupa Registration — Legal review (redline attached)

Tessa / Rishi / Jill —

I reviewed Redlined-MSA-v3.pdf. High-level: the requested Net-45 in the payment clause is not a deal-breaker from a commercial risk perspective, but CuraHealth's standard Net-30 is reasonable for cashflow and we should avoid establishing a broad Net-45 precedent without stronger credit controls.

Practical proposals (pick one):
- Option A (preferred): Accept Net-30 in the MSA and add an Order Form note: "Customer and Vendor agree to Net-45 for the first two invoices only as an invoicing exception; thereafter Net-30 applies." That keeps the long-term baseline at Net-30 while granting the short-term flexibility CuraHealth needs.
- Option B (alternative): Keep Net-45 but require a guarantee: (i) automatic ACH payment on invoice presentment after day 30; or (ii) 1% early-pay discount if paid by day 20.

If CuraHealth prefers Option A we can produce a one-page amendment for signature today. I've attached a suggested redline excerpt (Redlined-MSA-Payment-Excerpt.pdf) that implements Option A.  

I recommend we also include a line in the Order Form: "Vendor setup in purchasing system contingent on executed agreement and valid vendor tax ID matching W-9." That addresses procurement's registration gating.

Happy to chat for 15 minutes if you want to finalize language.

-Marcus Lin
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redlined-MSA-Payment-Excerpt.pdf (PDF, 1 page)
